summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands on embedded systems and firmware experience across STM32 microcontrollers, Arduino, and Raspberry Pi platforms. Built bare-metal C firmware exercising GPIO, timers, ADC, and I2C, fabricated custom PCBs in EAGLE, and implemented UART, I2C, and SPI sensor communication with closed-loop motor control across multiple robotics projects. Comfortable debugging hardware with oscilloscopes, multimeters, and logic analyzers, and working in Linux environments for embedded development.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating an ADXL345 accelerometer with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition in a laboratory environment, using GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for technical documentation.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) on an STM32 Cortex-M4; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: Robocon Competition Robot — Holonomic Drive & Encoder Odometry
bullets: Built closed-loop heading correction for a 4-wheel holonomic robot on Arduino Due: derived actual heading from dual-axis quadrature encoder odometry (2400 CPR, 2.9 cm wheels) and fed angular error back into rotation PWM, holding course during translation.
Implemented interrupt-driven quadrature decoding from first principles, a 4-bit A/B transition state machine on hardware interrupts, and drove four motor channels at 15 kHz PWM via DuePWM.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on a Linux-based NVIDIA Jetson host to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 microcontroller over UART.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X time-of-flight sensing and OLED distance visualization.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
